newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 21.

text.p: A man calling himself a Satan worshipper attacked detective Brent Garner and left him to die in his petrol-soaked house because Garner was a fighter against evil, police psychologist Ian Miller said on Sunday. Page 1.

Former NZ First strategist Michael Laws on Sunday tipped National as the likely coalition partner, pointing to the Alliance as a big problem in striking a deal with Labour. NZ First begins its coalition talks with National today and with Labour on Wednesday. "At the end of the day NZ First will go
with the party that delivers most of its policy agenda," said Laws. Page 1.

The ambiguous result of the New Zealand election should provide Britons with enough evidence to reject proportional representation as an unrealistic way to govern, according to The Economist. In a regular column, the magazine reported the state of New Zealand politics as a disaster and said all democratic societies should fear it. Page 2.

Wellington region manufacturers expect to boost sales in the next quarter after a disappointing three months to September, according to a survey commissioned by Wellington Regional Council. A net 10 percent of manufacturers reported a fall in domestic sales in the September quarter. Page 13.

Evergreen Forest's share option plan for executives came under fire at the company's annual meeting in Auckland last week. There was doubt about whether the plan would actually induce directors to produce a better share performance. Page 14.

Up to 65 percent of small holdings in ostrich farming in Australia and New Zealand could go out of business in the next 18 months, according to Peter Webb, chairman of the southern hemisphere's largest ostrich farming company, Afro Ostrich Farms. Page 14.

The torture inflicted on a Palmerston North policeman left for dead in his home lends weight to the view that some people are just plain evil, police and experts on the criminal mind say. They say the attack on detective Brent Garner is probably
the first of its type in New Zealand. Page 1.

The Royal New Zealand Navy is unlikely to get another two frigates regardless of who leads a coalition government, say defence analysts. They say the defence force is in danger of sliding well below the "credible minimum" demanded by the 1991 defence white paper and expected by Australia and Asia.

The serious business of forming the first MMP government starts today when New Zealand First and National Party negotiating teams sit down at an undisclosed neutral location. Members of National and Labour have been given instructions not to speak about any aspect of the talks in case they jeopardise their negotiating position with New Zealand First.
The Alliance candidate for Mangere Len Richards added his voice to criticism of the party's poor election showing saying getting 10 percent of the vote was "a serious reversal for us".

Unsuccessful Te Tai Tokerau candidate Dick Dargaville is again considering his future with the National Party. Dargaville was heavily defeated in the election, polling fewer than 500 votes. He said on Sunday National no longer had a mandate to represent Maori.
